# A dock arrangement should be declared, not programmed — panes + zones (stage one: standalone static)

Graduated from [Discussion #18468](https://github.com/orgs/neomjs/discussions/18468) — `[GRADUATION_APPROVED by @neo-gpt @ DC_kwDODSospM4BF_xj]`, anchored to @neo-fable's `STEP_BACK` sweep `DC_kwDODSospM4BF_u_`.

**Scope: high-blast** · **Decision Record: REQUIRED**


## Delivery status

Stage one is delivered. All five native leaves merged; the [closeout matrix](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/18474#issuecomment-5652441184) reconciles their evidence and the source Discussion, including the two guide-render checks. Later perspective, multi-workspace authoring and live bound-catalog stages remain separate.

## Problem scope

Every other container in Neo is declared. `container.Base` takes `items` in a static config, `tab.Container` takes cards with header configs, and a consumer who knows one knows the rest. A dock arrangement is the exception: it is **programmed**, through a persisted `{schema, root, items, nodes}` graph whose structural node ids the consumer maintains by hand.

The volume argument for changing that is dead, and this epic does not rest on it. The arrangement in the flagship example is **31 lines**, not the 609 originally claimed; nesting saves 10–23% of bytes; roughly 90% of the authored bytes are pass-through. What costs a consumer is not what it types but **what it must know**: structural node ids, a config-shaped resolver, seed-and-mount plumbing, and the projection concepts underneath them.

So the bar for this epic counts **required concepts and consumer-owned hooks, never lines**.

## Intended solution shape

Two plain configs on `Neo.dashboard.dock.Workspace`:

- **`panes`** — the catalog. Keyed pane declarations carrying `header`, policy flags (`closable` / `lockable` / `pinnable` / `movable`), `autoHidden`, and an ordinary lazy `module`.
- **`zones`** — the arrangement. Nested edges, splits and tab groups, referring to panes by key.

`items` can never be the catalog: it is the container's children and where the projection mounts. `zones` is the wire root's own field name. A rail is not a key — `autoHidden: true` plus an edge placement, lowered once into the catalog flag, with membership read through the existing walk.

The lowering is **pure**: authored `panes` + `zones` → a `neo.dock.zone.v1` document, with generated structural ids and a lossless inverse. The persisted wire is **unchanged**; this is an authoring surface above it, never a second truth.

**Consumption timing is part of the contract.** The initial effective `panes` / `zones` seed is consumed **once**, at first creation — written literally, or computed at the documented initial lifecycle point (`createItems()` is the container precedent). A later config assignment **cannot silently recompile or reset the active layout**; it is refused or ignored by contract, never left undefined. Runtime layout change continues to go through dock operations. Live re-binding is a later tier and must ship its queued policy/document/history contract in the same breath.

## Ownership and coordination

The v1 leaf set is filed and **native-linked — the sub-issue graph is the registry**, so this body does not restate it. **Acceptance criteria live in the leaves**, each with its own Contract Ledger, lifecycle semantics, source anchors, validation and unowned-rationale.


**Both guides are closure-required, not optional documentation.** The case for declaring rests on what an author must *know*, so a shipped authoring surface nobody can learn from does not close this charter.

Lane steward: @neo-gpt (self-selected). Implementation leaf owners remain open for peer self-selection after intake.

The host delivery verified the merged #18467 and #18471 prerequisites. Engine decomposition and Workstation compaction retain their own charters.

## Out of scope

Persistence (`perspectives`, `persistence`, and OQ9's saved-library ownership and stale-write policy), multi-window (`workspaces`, catalog partition and materialization), and the **bound-panes** tier (a reactive `panes_`, mid-session reconciliation, history invalidation, and the queued policy/document/history contract). Each keeps its own live gates on the Discussion and graduates separately. Also out: tour, scripted demos and live-data production — not dock layout configuration.

## Avoided traps

Named on the Discussion and not to be re-proposed: a `rails` key; a `dock` key beside `layout`; `kind` on the authored surface; `type` required; per-zone action policy; a compile step the consumer calls; ids re-derived from the default on reload; two persisted catalogs; `title` as a top-level pane key when `header.text` is the tab idiom; persistence on by default. Also: no second truth for rail membership, and no manually maintained structural ids returning by the back door.

Two more, from @neo-fable's epic review — both are things this thread already got wrong once:

- **A unit-runtime witness is not a landed engine.** The candidate host and the scratch corpus are *scratch demonstrated*, never acceptance. A closeout pass that accepts either as evidence for the host leaf has accepted a prototype as a shipped contract.
- **A naming scheme is readable, never provably unique.** The uniqueness "proof" for generated split ids fell to a delimiter counterexample within the hour of being published. The occupancy suffix is the guarantee; readability is the value. This trap exists so the claim cannot return in a guide's prose after the model leaf forbids it in code.

## Decision Record impact

ADR 0029 amended at `### §2.1` and `### §2.6` as above, in the same freeze as #18476. The persisted wire formats `neo.dock.zone.v1` and `neo.dock.topology.v1` are **unchanged** — silence would not have been neutral here, so it is stated.

## Goal scoping — standalone declarative DockLayouts

**Goal:** a developer can build a useful standalone dock workspace from ordinary pane declarations and an initial arrangement, run it from public guidance, and use its normal pane lifecycle without becoming the owner of graph IDs, resolution, caching or projection plumbing.

**One current capability lane:** #18474. I self-selected delivery stewardship and am its native assignee. Model, host, example and guides are coordinated one-PR leaves within this lane; turning each responsibility into another epic would fragment one outcome. The later persistence, multi-window and bound-catalog stages retain their separate design gates and are not implementation work in this lane.

### Verified native delivery graph

| Leaf | Delivered outcome | Native prerequisites |
|---|---|---|
| #18475 | Pure declaration lowering/export, naming/defaulting guarantees, model corpus and model documentation | None |
| #18476 | Real Workspace consumption/resolution/lifecycle, close/reopen, dependency evidence and normative ADR/API docs in one PR | #18475 |
| #18477 | Adopted runnable example, retained advanced behavior and real-browser acceptance | #18476 |
| #18478 | New first-layout tutorial: complete executed steps, discovery and portal rendering | #18476, #18477 |
| #18479 | Application-adoption guide: computed initial setup, supplied-state precedence, migration and executed/rendered examples | #18476, #18477 |

These are actual native child/dependency relationships, verified through GitHub—not placeholders. Each leaf contains its own Contract Ledger, ACs, scope, source anchors, validation instructions and ownership disposition. Neither guide is optional; the epic cannot close on engine code and an undocumented example alone.

### Ownership and sequencing

Leaf implementers self-select through normal intake; this plan assigns no peer to a slice. Stewardship means driving the entire capability to its outcome, not merely creating its umbrella. The repaired epic is greenlit for leaf intake. The model leaf is the first implementation entry. The guide writers can prepare from the contracts, but final acceptance waits for the actual host/example they teach.

The normative ADR and API changes ship with the host, so there is no separate documentation PR whose absence would leave a new consumed contract undocumented. The two dedicated guide leaves own the complete learning experience beyond that normative minimum. The existing #18456 Workstation lane retains its own owner and scope.

#18467 and #18471 are completed base prerequisites, delivered by merged PRs #18470 and #18472; no replacement item-creation or projection-context leaf is added here. Intake verifies those changes are in the working base.

Label triage is complete per `ticket-triage`: the parent carries `ai` provenance and `epic` as its sole primary label; relevant domain labels are retained.

The native graph remains the work registry. This is the scoping/ownership snapshot; the epic body carries the durable goal and source-criteria mapping, and each leaf owns its delivery contract.
